comparisons.peer_topic: Noninterest expense increase drivers and prior year comparisons
comparisons.peer_summary: Noninterest expense increased $967 million to $66.8 billion in 2024 compared to 2023, primarily driven by higher revenue-related expenses and investments in people, operations, and technology, partially offset by higher FDIC expense in 2023 (including a $2.1 billion special assessment) and lower expenses from a liquidating business activity.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures highlight the financial impact of specific banking sector events on expenses, though the drivers differ. JPMorgan focuses on the integration phase of the First Republic acquisition, noting substantial completion of operations conversion as of year-end 2024. In contrast, Bank of America details how its noninterest expense in 2024 was partially offset by higher FDIC expenses in the prior year (2023) specifically related to the closures of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank. While both reference FDIC-related costs or activities, JPM's disclosure centers on the operational integration of an acquired entity (First Republic), whereas Bank of America's disclosure centers on expense normalization after absorbing special assessments from peer bank failures.

sentences.text: As of December 31, 2024, the Firm had substantially completed the conversion of operations, and the integration of clients, products and services, associated with the First Republic acquisition to align with the Firm's businesses and operations.

The increase was primarily driven by higher revenue-related expenses as well as investments in people, operations and technology, partially offset by higher Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) expense in 2023, including $2.1 billion for the estimated special assessment amount arising from the closure of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank, and lower expenses related to a liquidating business activity.
